_about: Cook with Nani: which hand pose goes with which action (js/cook/hands.js). The hands are the baked character skins (assets/characters/hands/skins/<character>/hand-<file>.webp, hands v3); build/hands_webp.py makes the game-sized copies in assets/cook/hands/<character>/ (trimmed, scaled by `scale`, webp) and data/hand-sprites.json (crop, size and where the arm leaves the bottom edge). Coordinates here are pixels in the skin image. poses: id -> {file, tip: the action point (a fingertip, the gap of a pinch or grab, the grip of a tool), tool: for a grip, {at: where the tool's grip sits, dir: the direction the tool points from there, degrees, 0 = up the frame, clockwise}}. actions: what a mechanic asks for -> the frames it plays (one pose, or a sequence played frame to frame). stations: the poses a station preloads (only those load, so a phone keeps a few textures) and the action a tap on a station's thing gets by default (`tap`: an action name; null = no hand). Nani's hands (her skins, `nani`) come in from the top edge: she's across the worktop. Where no pose fits, there is no hand (the behaviour before hands).
scale_note: master px -> 1600x900 design px: the 250 px master forearm is 100 design px, about a bowl's width over 1.7

tap._what: a tap on a thing, a knob, a timing ring: the pointing finger presses it

pick._what: pick up an item (the pantry, a dough bowl): open hand, then it closes on the item

pinch._what: a pinch of sugar, masala, a topping; a piece to thread

pour._what: a tap on the jug: the hand hooks its handle and tilts

carry._what: carry a bowl or a cup: two hands

give._what: hand the dish to a customer (two hands up to them)

fold._what: the samosa fold swipe: the two-hand pinch fold follows the finger

count._what: counting on fingers: frame n shows n (what you've done, never the target)

tool._what: a knife, ladle, spatula or slotted spoon in the b1 handle grip, the tool on its own layer under the fingers

roll._what: two hands on the rolling pin (the pin is still drawn: the velan failed batch 1's QA)

nani-receive._what: Nani holds her hand out for what she asked for (pass me)

nani-show._what: Nani's see-through finger shows a move (the hint demo when you haven't started)

tools._about: Tools held in the grip (S.hand(tool)): the painted tool (data.art.sprites.tools) lies along the grip's handle axis, `len` design px long, gripped `grip` of the way from its tip; `angle` is added to the angle the mechanic asks for (the old drawn hand held its tool straight up; the painted grip holds it across, to the thumb side).
